352629.title: 3-dimensional Rota Conjecture
352629.literal_statement:
Let $V$ be a vector space over an arbitrary infinite field with $\dim V=n^2$. Suppose $B_1,\ldots,B_n$ are $n$ sets of bases of $V$. For each $i$, choose a linear ordering of $B_i$, writing $B_i=\{b_{ijk}\mid j,k\in[n]\}$. **3-dimensional Rota Conjecture.** The sets

$$
C_j=\{b_{ijk}\mid i,k\in[n]\}\quad (j\in[n]),
$$

and

$$
D_k=\{b_{ijk}\mid i,j\in[n]\}\quad (k\in[n])
$$

are each $n$ sets of bases of $V$. The supplied text gives no resolution.

352633.title: Corteel--Dousse--Uncu positivity conjecture for arbitrary-rank cylindric partitions
352633.literal_statement:
For integers $d,r\geqslant1$, let $c=(c_0,\dots,c_{r-1})$ be a profile of level $d$, meaning

$$
c_0+\cdots+c_{r-1}=d.
$$

Let $Q_{n,c}(q)$ be the formal power series defined from the cylindric-partition generating function by the source's formula. **Arbitrary-rank cylindric-partition positivity conjecture.** The series $Q_{n,c}(q)$ is a polynomial in $q$ with nonnegative coefficients and

$$
Q_{n,c}(1)=\left(\frac{\gcd(d,r)}{d+r}\binom{d+r}{r}-\gcd(d,r)\right)^n.
$$

This generalises the rank-$3$ conjecture of Corteel, Dousse and Uncu and is motivated by the expected interpolation between finite-rank Andrews--Gordon identities; the supplied context does not state a proof.

352695.title: Odd-homology vanishing conjecture for moduli spaces of planar trivalent graphs
352695.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a planar trivalent graph, and let $\mathcal{M}(G)$ be the moduli space of admissible decorations of $G$: each edge $e$ is assigned a point $D(e)\in\mathbb{CP}^2$, and at every vertex the decorations on the three incident edges are pairwise orthogonal. For an integer $i$, write $H_i(\mathcal{M}(G))$ for the $i$-th homology group of this moduli space.

**Odd-homology vanishing conjecture.** For any planar trivalent graph $G$ and for $i$ odd, one has

$$
H_i(\mathcal{M}(G))=0.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by an earlier conjecture cited in the source. The source does not establish the vanishing for all planar trivalent graphs.

352741.title: The interior-vertex lower-bound conjecture for grid pebbling distributions
352741.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a solvable pebbling distribution on the grid. A vertex is **interior** if it does not lie on the boundary of the grid.

**Interior-vertex lower-bound conjecture.** For every interior vertex $X$,

$$
v(X) \geq \frac{3}{2}.
$$

The conjecture would improve the lower bound used in the paper from $\frac{4}{3}$ to $\frac{3}{2}$ for vertices away from the boundary, potentially yielding a stronger lower bound on the pebbling number of the grid. The source presents it as an open problem motivated by the observation about $2$-reachable vertices.

352811.title: Two-terminal-pair multicut dominant description conjecture
352811.literal_statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph and let $S$ be a set of terminal pairs with $|S|=2$. The **multicut dominant** $\textsc{MultC}(G,S)$ is the dominant associated with multicut incidence vectors. **Two-pair description conjecture.** It is completely described by

$$
x_e\geq 0\quad\text{for all }e\in E,
$$

and

$$
\sum_{e\in(P)}x_e\geq 1
$$

for each $s$-$t$ path $P$ with $\{s,t\}\in S$. The claim would extend the known complete description for one terminal pair; the source presents the two-pair case as an open conjecture, while more efficient separation methods remain separate open questions.

353018.title: The prime-field cylinder conjecture
353018.literal_statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $v,r$ be positive integers, and consider $q^r$-divisible sets of $q^{r+1}$ points in the projective space $\operatorname{PG}(v-1,q)$, subject to the cylinder-conjecture setting described in the source. A cylinder is the corresponding affine configuration obtained after choosing an empty hyperplane.

**Prime-field cylinder conjecture.** The cylinder conjecture is true for all parameter triples $(v,r,p)$, where $p$ is a prime.

The claim concerns the classification of divisible sets of $q^{r+1}$ points; the surrounding text states that it is known in several low-dimensional or small-field cases and can fail for suitable nonprime fields because of subfield cylinders. No resolution is given for all prime field sizes.

356576.title: Quantum causal correlations conjecture for chordless siblings-on-cycles graphs
356576.literal_statement: Let $W$ be a quantum process with causal structure $G=(V,E)$. A process produces causal correlations when, for every collection of local experiments $\mu$, the resulting correlations $p(a\mid x)$ are causal. **Quantum causal correlations conjecture.** If $G$ is a chordless siblings-on-cycles graph, then $W$ always produces causal correlations. The corresponding statement is proved for classical-deterministic processes by reducing successively at source nodes. Whether every quantum process on a chordless siblings-on-cycles graph produces only causal correlations remains open.

356912.title: Kajitani, Ueno and Miyano's conjecture on cyclically orderable graphs
356912.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. Its **density** is

$$
d(G)=\frac{|E(G)|}{|V(G)|-1}.
$$

The graph $G$ is **uniformly dense** if $d(H)\leq d(G)$ for every connected subgraph $H$ of $G$. A graph is **cyclically orderable** if it has a cyclic ordering of its edges such that every cyclically consecutive $|V(G)|-1$ edges induce a spanning tree. **Kajitani, Ueno and Miyano's conjecture.** A connected graph $G$ is cyclically orderable if and only if it is uniformly dense. This gives a density-theoretic characterization of cyclic base orderings; the source states that the necessity was proved by Kajitani, Ueno and Miyano, while the converse is the conjectural direction.

345220.title: Disjoint base-block conjecture for cyclic $(v,k,1)$-designs
345220.literal_statement: Let $(V,\mathcal{B})$ be a cyclic $(v,k,1)$-design: the blocks are partitioned into orbits under a cyclic automorphism, and a base block is one chosen block from each orbit. **Disjoint base-block conjecture.** For every cyclic $(v,k,1)$-design, one can choose one block from each block orbit so that all chosen blocks are pairwise disjoint. This extends the Steiner triple system case to arbitrary block size $k$ and allows short orbits; the paper proves the assertion when $v$ is prime, but leaves the general case conjectural.

345283.title: Persistence of divots in missing-difference distributions
345283.literal_statement:
Let $P_n^{\mathrm{H}}(k)$ denote the probability distribution associated with the relevant diffset statistic, and call $k$ a **divot** of this distribution when it is a local depression. Let $n_1$ be a positive integer.

**Divot persistence conjecture.** If $k$ is a divot of $P_{n_1}^{\mathrm{H}}$, then $k$ is also a divot of $P_n^{\mathrm{H}}$ for every $n>n_1$.

This conjecture asserts that once a divot appears, its location never changes as $n$ increases. The source gives no resolution status.

345327.title: The critical one-half conjecture for circle packings
345327.literal_statement:
Let $4\mathcal{S}4$ be a circle packing and let $s_0\in\mathcal{S}$. For $0<p<1$, let $E_{\mathcal{S},p}(s_0,r)$ denote the event that $s_0$ is connected to distance $r$ by open disks, and let $E_{\mathcal{S},p}(s_0,\infty)$ denote the event that it is connected to infinity. **The critical one-half conjecture for circle packings.**

$$
\mathbb{P}(E_{\mathcal{S},1/2}(s_0,\infty))=0.
$$

This would imply absence of infinite components at $p=1/2$ for several classes of planar graphs, including recurrent simple plane triangulations and suitable Benjamini–Schramm limits. It remains open even for triangulation circle packings with carrier $\mathbb{R}^2$ and uniformly bounded disk radii.

345332.title: Formula for runs of a fixed part and length in compositions
345332.literal_statement:
Let $R(n,k,l)$ denote the number of runs of $k$ of length $l$ over all compositions of $n$, and let $a(1,m)$ be the corresponding two-toned tiling count, interpreted as zero when its second argument is negative. **The run-count formula.** For all $n,k,l$,

$$
R(n,k,l)=a(1,n-kl)-2a(1,n-(l+1)k)+a(1,n-(l+2)k).
$$

This gives an explicit relation between refined run counts in compositions and two-toned tiling numbers; the supplied context does not indicate that the formula is open or conjectural.

345349.title: Wang's arbitrary cycle-factor conjecture for graphs
345349.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, and let $W\subseteq V(G)$ be a vertex set. For a positive integer $k$, an **arbitrary $W$-cycle-factor** is a collection of $k$ disjoint cycles $C_1,\ldots,C_k$ satisfying $|V(C_i)\cap W|=n_i$ for a prescribed partition $|W|=n_1+\cdots+n_k$, with each $n_i\geq 3$.

**Wang's conjecture.** If $|W|\geq 3k$ and $\delta(W)\geq 2n/3$, then $G$ contains an arbitrary $W$-cycle-factor.

This conjecture generalizes the arbitrary 2-factor theorem of Aigner and Brandt to a specified vertex set. Its status is not established in the source.

345506.title: The hypergraph–QLR cone equality conjecture
345506.literal_statement: For each $n$, let the $n$-party hypergraph cone be the cone of entropy vectors obtained from $n$-party hypergraphs, and let the $n$-party QLR cone be the cone defined by the quantum linear rank inequalities. **Hypergraph–QLR cone conjecture.** The $n$-party hypergraph and QLR cones coincide for all $n$. The cones are known to coincide through four parties, and the paper gives contraction-map evidence for five parties; equality in general would identify the hypergraph cone with a cone of quantum-compatible entropy vectors.

345734.title: Injectivity conjecture for discrete homotopy and homology of the graphs $G_n$
345734.literal_statement:
Let $G_1$ be a cycle graph of length $5$, and let $G_n$ be the graphs defined recursively in the source via the discrete suspension construction. For each $n$, let $\psi:A_n(G_n)\to \hc_n(G_n)$ be the natural homomorphism from discrete homotopy to discrete singular cubical homology. **Injectivity conjecture for $G_n$.** The map $\psi$ is injective for all $n$.

The theorem preceding this conjecture establishes surjectivity in the relevant family, so injectivity would make $\psi$ an isomorphism for every $n$. The conjecture is motivated by the analogy between $G_n$ and the sphere $S^n$.

345742.title: The list Unfriendly Partition Conjecture for countable graphs
345742.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a countable graph, and assign to each vertex $v$ a list $L(v)$ of available colors. The graph is **majority $k$-choosable** if, for every such assignment with $|L(v)|=k$, it has a majority coloring using a color from $L(v)$ at each vertex, where at each vertex the number of incident monochromatic edges is at most the number of incident edges whose endpoints have different colors. **List Unfriendly Partition Conjecture.** Every countable graph is majority $2$-choosable. This strengthens the Unfriendly Partition Conjecture. The paper proves the weaker bound that every countable graph is majority $4$-choosable, so the conjectured bound remains open.

345744.title: The list 2-coloring conjecture for countable acyclic digraphs
345744.literal_statement: Let $D$ be a countable acyclic digraph, and assign to each vertex $v$ a list $L(v)$ of available colors. The digraph is **majority $k$-choosable** if, for every such assignment with $|L(v)|=k$, it has a majority coloring using a color from $L(v)$ at each vertex, where at every vertex at most half of its outgoing edges are bad. **Acyclic digraph list-coloring conjecture.** Every countable acyclic digraph is majority $2$-choosable. The greedy algorithm proves the analogous statement for finite acyclic digraphs, but the countable list version is left open.

345784.title: The Log-span conjecture
345784.literal_statement:
Let $V$ be a finite set such that, for every $k\leq\operatorname{dim} V$, every $k$-dimensional subset of $V$ has at most $2^k$ elements.

**Log-span conjecture.**

$$
\beta(V)=|V|,
$$

and in particular

$$
\alpha(V)\geq |V|^{1/2}.
$$

This conjecture would follow from the linear matroid conjecture together with the theorem for subsets of quasicubes; it extends the sharp tripling bound known for quasicubes to a broader class of sets.

345785.title: The linear matroid conjecture for induced tripling
345785.literal_statement:
Let $U$ and $V$ be finite sets of equal cardinality in a group, and let $\varphi:U\to V$ be a bijection. For every subset $U'\subset U$, compare the dimensions of its image and itself.

**Linear matroid conjecture.** If

$$
\operatorname{dim}\varphi(U')\leq \operatorname{dim}U'
$$

for every $U'\subset U$, then

$$
\beta(V)\leq\beta(U).
$$

In particular, if $\operatorname{dim}\varphi(U')=\operatorname{dim}U'$ for every $U'\subset U$, then $\beta(V)=\beta(U)$. This conjecture asserts that induced tripling is controlled by the linear dependence matroid; the Log-span conjecture would follow from it and the quasicube theorem.
